title: Modelling Structures for Situated Discourse
research_question: How should discourse structure be modeled when multiparty linguistic moves interact with nonlinguistic events in a situated environment, including structures that cannot be represented as a simple tree?
methodology: The authors compare two discourse annotations of STAC, a corpus of multiparty chat from an online Settlers of Catan environment: an initial chat-only annotation and a later situated annotation that also represents game events. Chats are segmented into elementary discourse units and linked with SDRT-style rhetorical relations, while complex discourse units can group several elementary units into a single relational argument. Four initially naive annotators were trained on 22 negotiation dialogues comprising 560 turns, followed by four expert annotators and at least five revision stages that produced consensus gold annotations. The paper quantitatively compares attachments and structures between the linguistic-only and situated versions of the corpus.

key_findings.finding: Responses can have multiple distinct antecedents: in one analyzed exchange, a single acknowledgement is interpreted as responding jointly to three preceding negative replies.

Such multi-antecedent links are not rare in this corpus: 928 of 12,588 discourse units in the chat-only annotations, about 7%, are classified as truly non-treelike because they receive incoming links from different source units.
The corpus contains simultaneously developing dialogue threads, and even an individual speaker can participate in several independent threads at once.

Offers and their acceptances or refusals are modeled propositionally through Question-Answer Pair relations: a completed trade can function as a yes to an offer, while a trade-panel refusal or rejection functions as a no.

Complex discourse units allow several antecedent events or replies to be treated jointly as the argument of a later relation; for example, an action can be annotated as the result of an entire sequence of failed offers and refusals rather than of one immediately preceding unit.
key_findings.section: 3.1.2 Complex structures relevant for the situated annotations

key_findings.finding: Adding situated events supplied antecedents for all 1,501 chat-only orphan units and created 3,591 links between linguistic and nonlinguistic material.

Local relation preservation was substantially higher than whole-structure preservation: persisting chat-only relations made up 72% of situated chat-to-chat relations, while only 496 of 1,137 chat-only dialogue structures, a little over 43%, were preserved as elementary substructures.
key_findings.section: 4.1 Preservation of relations; 4.2 Preservation of structures

key_findings.finding: Pilot annotation agreement was kappa 0.72 for attachment alone and 0.58 when exact attachment and relation label both had to match.

limitations: The interaction domain is a strategy game rather than workplace email or enterprise collaboration.
The paper is primarily about discourse structure and situated context, not specifically about unanswered subquestions in compound interrogatives.
Its strongest evidence for joint antecedents concerns multiparty chat and game actions, so transfer to asynchronous email requires empirical validation.
The interpretation of complex and non-treelike attachments depends on SDRT annotation decisions and expert consensus.
Initial attachment-plus-label agreement was only moderate at kappa 0.58 before expert revision.
The represented nonlinguistic context is derived from the game environment and does not encompass every kind of real-world contextual state relevant to workplace communication.
raw_claims: STAC contains multiparty chat situated in an online Settlers of Catan environment.
Discourse units are connected by directed rhetorical relations rather than being constrained to a tree.
A truly non-treelike unit can be linked to two or more different antecedent discourse units.
The chat-only data contain 928 truly non-treelike units among 12,588 discourse units.
One acknowledgement in the corpus is analyzed as jointly addressing three preceding negative responses.
Independent conversational threads can proceed simultaneously.
Offers are represented as structures that can receive acceptance or refusal responses.
A rejection in the game interface can serve the discourse function of a negative answer to an offer.
Several events can be grouped into one complex discourse unit and jointly serve as an antecedent.
Adding game events changes a substantial fraction of discourse attachments inferred from language alone.
The STAC annotations and their annotation manual are linked from the paper.
